claims: Cancer is a group of diseases characterized by uncontrolled cell growth caused by DNA alterations.
Uncontrolled cell growth in cancer results in tumors or blood cancers.
Cancer can spread (metastasize).
Cancer is diagnosed through imaging, biopsies, and blood tests.
Cancer is treated with surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy.
CT scans, MRIs, PET scans, and X-rays are commonly used imaging tests for cancer diagnosis, notes the Mayo Clinic.
Biopsy involves taking a small sample of tissue for examination, says MedlinePlus.
Biopsy is a definitive method for cancer diagnosis, says MedlinePlus.
Laboratory tests for cancer include blood or urine tests that look for specific cancer cells or tumor markers, according to MedlinePlus.
Endoscopy procedures and physical exams are used to look inside the body and detect abnormalities for cancer diagnosis, explains National Cancer Institute.
Cancer surgery involves removing the tumor, says Wikipedia.
Chemotherapy uses drugs to kill cancer cells, according to Wikipedia.
Radiation therapy uses high-dose radiation to kill cancer cells, notes Wikipedia.
Targeted therapy and immunotherapy for cancer target specific genetic changes or boost the immune system, explains Wikipedia.
CAR-T cell therapy engineers a patient's own T-cells to attack cancer, says a YouTube video from the National Cancer Institute.
Precision medicine involves developing treatments tailored to the specific genetic makeup of a tumor, notes the World Health Organization.
Liquid biopsies detect cancer through blood tests to identify circulating tumor DNA.
Liquid biopsies allow for earlier diagnosis and monitoring of cancer.
Artificial intelligence is used in cancer diagnosis to improve the accuracy and speed of imaging interpretation, notes the World Health Organization.
Tobacco use is the leading cause of cancer, says Cancer Progress Report.
Tobacco use accounts for a significant portion of cancer deaths, says Cancer Progress Report.
Cancer risk factors from lifestyle and environment include obesity, poor diet, lack of exercise, alcohol, and UV radiation, say Wikipedia and the VCU Massey Comprehensive Cancer Center.
Viruses such as HPV and Hepatitis are risk factors for cancer, according to the World Health Organization.
